Set tolerances and switches for MS filtering

mc_ms_parameters.Rd

Create a complete named list of MS-filter settings, replacing selected defaults with your named arguments.

mc_ms_parameters(...)

Arguments

...

Named settings to replace. Supported names, meanings, units, and defaults are listed below. Unknown names raise an error.

Details

Pass the returned list to mc_filter_ms(parameters = ...). Merely creating the list does not change any analysis. All RT tolerances are in minutes. Da and ppm tolerances are alternatives selected separately for each subfilter. Explicit filter names in mc_filter_ms() override the enable flags.

enable_iso2

Enable isotope filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An explicit filters vector overrides this flag; use "isotopes" to select isotope filtering explicitly. Default: TRUE.

iso_cor2

Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of a candidate isotope and its parent feature. Values range from 0 to 1; higher cutoffs require more similar profiles. Default: 0.8.

iso_rt2

Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between a candidate isotope and its parent feature. Default: 0.01.

iso_tol_type2

Mass-tolerance unit for isotope matching: "da" uses iso_mz_tol2; "ppm" uses iso_ppm2. Only the selected tolerance is used. Default: da.

iso_mz_tol2

Absolute mass tolerance in Da for isotope matching. Used only when iso_tol_type2 = "da". Default: 0.005.

iso_ppm2

Relative mass tolerance in ppm for isotope matching. Used only when iso_tol_type2 = "ppm". Default: 10.

iso_zmax2

Maximum charge state searched for isotope relationships. For example, 3 searches charge states 1, 2 and 3. Default: 3.

iso_n2

Maximum isotope order k searched. Expected isotope spacing is 1.00336 * k / z Da, for orders 1 through iso_n2 and charges 1 through iso_zmax2. Default: 1.

iso_nd2

Number of additional dimer-pattern isotope shifts searched: 1.00336 * (j + 0.5) Da for j from 1 through iso_nd2. Default: 3.

enable_add2

Enable adduct filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An explicit filters vector overrides this flag; use "adducts" to select adduct filtering explicitly. Default: TRUE.

add_pol2

Ionization polarity used to select adduct definitions: "positive" or "negative". Set nl_pol2 separately if neutral-loss filtering is also used. Default: positive.

add_cor2

Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of features proposed to belong to the same adduct family. Values range from 0 to 1; higher cutoffs require more similar profiles. Default: 0.8.

add_rt2

Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between features proposed to belong to the same adduct family. Default: 0.005.

add_tol_type2

Mass-tolerance unit for adduct matching: "da" uses add_mz_tol2; "ppm" uses add_ppm2. Only the selected tolerance is used. Default: da.

add_mz_tol2

Absolute mass tolerance in Da for adduct matching. Used only when add_tol_type2 = "da". Default: 0.005.

add_ppm2

Relative mass tolerance in ppm for adduct matching. Used only when add_tol_type2 = "ppm". Default: 10.

add_min_nm2

Minimum candidate neutral mass in Da for adduct annotation. Candidate neutral masses must be strictly greater than this threshold. Default: 50.

add_strict_rt2

If TRUE, restrict the total retention-time spread of an adduct family to add_rt2 minutes, in addition to pairwise matching. Default: TRUE.

add_prefer2

Prefer selected ion forms when choosing adduct-family representatives. Retain the most intense qualifying preferred feature, or the most intense feature overall if none qualify. Default: FALSE.

add_preferred2

Character vector of preferred ion names, matching the adduct definitions exactly. Default: NULL, using "M+H" for positive polarity or "M-H" for negative polarity. For example, c("M+H", "M+Na") prefers features with at least one assignment matching either ion form, without priority ordering.

add_prefer_pct2

Maximum intensity decrease (%) from the family's highest mean intensity for a preferred representative. Default: 10; range: 0--100.

enable_nl2

Enable neutral-loss filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An explicit filters vector overrides this flag; use "neutral_losses" to select neutral-loss filtering explicitly. Default: FALSE.

nl_pol2

Ionization polarity used to select neutral-loss definitions: "positive" or "negative". Set add_pol2 separately if adduct filtering is also used. Default: positive.

nl_cor2

Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of features proposed to differ by a listed neutral loss. Values range from 0 to 1; higher cutoffs require more similar profiles. Default: 0.95.

nl_rt2

Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between features proposed to differ by a listed neutral loss. Default: 0.002.

nl_tol_type2

Mass-tolerance unit for neutral-loss matching: "da" uses nl_mz_tol2; "ppm" uses nl_ppm2. Only the selected tolerance is used. Default: da.

nl_mz_tol2

Absolute mass tolerance in Da for neutral-loss matching. Used only when nl_tol_type2 = "da". Default: 0.005.

nl_ppm2

Relative mass tolerance in ppm for neutral-loss matching. Used only when nl_tol_type2 = "ppm". Default: 10.

enable_isf2

Enable in-source fragment filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An explicit filters vector overrides this flag; use "isf" to select in-source fragment filtering explicitly. Default: FALSE.

isf_cor2

Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of a candidate in-source fragment and its precursor feature. Values range from 0 to 1; higher cutoffs require more similar profiles. Default: 0.95.

isf_rt2

Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between a candidate in-source fragment and its precursor feature. Default: 0.01.

isf_control_int2

If TRUE, require the mean fragment/precursor intensity ratio to fall between isf_ratio_min2 and isf_ratio_max2. If FALSE, omit this intensity-ratio condition. Default: TRUE.

isf_ratio_min2

Lower allowed ratio of mean candidate fragment intensity to mean precursor intensity. Used when isf_control_int2 = TRUE. Default: 0.001.

isf_ratio_max2

Upper allowed ratio of mean candidate fragment intensity to mean precursor intensity. Used when isf_control_int2 = TRUE. Default: 2.5.

isf_ms2_check2

If TRUE, require the candidate fragment m/z in an eligible MS2 spectrum of the precursor; supply spectra to mc_filter_ms(). Support in any eligible spectrum is sufficient. FALSE uses MS1 evidence only. Default: TRUE.

isf_ms2_rel2

Minimum intensity of a supporting MS2 peak, expressed as a percentage of that spectrum's base peak. For example, 1 means 1 percent. Used when isf_ms2_check2 = TRUE. Default: 1.

isf_ms2_mz_tol2

Absolute tolerance in Da between the candidate in-source fragment m/z and a supporting MS2 peak. Used when isf_ms2_check2 = TRUE. Default: 0.01.

isf_mgf_id_field

Spectrum metadata field used to match MGF spectra to precursor feature IDs for in-source fragment checking; typically "acquisitionNum". Default: acquisitionNum.

enable_mis2

Enable mispicked-ion filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An explicit filters vector overrides this flag; use "mispicked" to select mispicked-ion filtering explicitly. Default: FALSE.

mis_cor2

Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of features proposed to be duplicate peak detections. Values range from 0 to 1; higher cutoffs require more similar profiles. Default: 0.8.

mis_rt2

Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between features proposed to be duplicate peak detections. Default: 0.002.

mis_tol_type2

Mass-tolerance unit for mispicked-ion matching: "da" uses mis_mz_tol2; "ppm" uses mis_ppm2. Only the selected tolerance is used. Default: ppm.

mis_mz_tol2

Absolute mass tolerance in Da for mispicked-ion matching. Used only when mis_tol_type2 = "da". Default: 0.005.

mis_ppm2

Relative mass tolerance in ppm for mispicked-ion matching. Used only when mis_tol_type2 = "ppm". Default: 10.

enable_ring2

Enable ringing/saturated-ion filtering when mc_filter_ms(filters = NULL). An explicit filters vector overrides this flag; use "ringing" to select ringing/saturated-ion filtering explicitly. Default: FALSE.

ring_cor2

Minimum Pearson correlation between the sample-intensity profiles of a candidate ringing artifact and its high-intensity anchor. Values range from 0 to 1; higher cutoffs require more similar profiles. Default: 0.8.

ring_rt2

Maximum retention-time difference, in minutes, between a candidate ringing artifact and its high-intensity anchor. Default: 0.05.

ring_tol_type2

Mass-tolerance unit for ringing/saturated-ion matching: "da" uses ring_mz_tol2; "ppm" uses ring_ppm2. Only the selected tolerance is used. Default: da.

ring_mz_tol2

Absolute mass tolerance in Da for ringing/saturated-ion matching. Used only when ring_tol_type2 = "da". Default: 0.95.

ring_ppm2

Relative mass tolerance in ppm for ringing/saturated-ion matching. Used only when ring_tol_type2 = "ppm". Default: 500.

ring_min_anch2

Minimum mean sample intensity for a feature to act as the high-intensity anchor in ringing/saturated-ion filtering. Default: 1e+05.

ring_ratio2

Minimum ratio of anchor mean intensity to candidate artifact mean intensity in ringing/saturated-ion filtering. For example, 10 requires the anchor to be at least ten times as intense; must be at least 1. Default: 10.

ring_bidirectional2

If TRUE, search for ringing artifacts below and above the anchor m/z. If FALSE, search only above the anchor m/z. Default: FALSE.

Value

A named list containing every MS parameter, including unchanged defaults.

See also

mc_filter_ms, mc_read_mgf

Examples

ms_options <- mc_ms_parameters(
  iso_rt2 = 0.01, iso_cor2 = 0.80,
  iso_tol_type2 = "da", iso_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  add_rt2 = 0.005, add_cor2 = 0.80,
  add_tol_type2 = "da", add_mz_tol2 = 0.005,
  add_pol2 = "positive",
  isf_rt2 = 0.01, isf_cor2 = 0.95,
  isf_ms2_check2 = TRUE, isf_ms2_mz_tol2 = 0.01,
  isf_ms2_rel2 = 1, isf_mgf_id_field = "acquisitionNum"
)
ms_options
